title: NASA Motor Vehicle Identification
slide_intent: Teach designers to judge a vehicle’s paint value against a reference scale. A middle-value door can make the choice of black or white lettering difficult by eye alone.
strategic_value: NASA can preserve readable identification across vehicles acquired in many colors and connect those choices to a common lettering arrangement.
demonstration: Instructions describe the government-use lines, logotype, agency and installation. A ten-step gray scale at right carries black or white type on each step, showing the switch at the 40% boundary.
practical_value: Match an uncertain paint color against the scale. Use black on a value of 40% or lighter and white above that value. Consider the separate red-logo option for a white vehicle.

content_islands.name: Vehicle markings and placement
content_islands.spec: Set the identification and placement instructions in the left text columns. Describe the front-door location, clearance from hardware, common left edge and circumstances for placing a larger logo elsewhere.

content_islands.name: Gray-scale comparator
content_islands.spec: Draw ten adjacent horizontal steps down the full right edge from dark to light. Print a type sample on each step so the contrast changes with the background.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text explains that a vehicle in the middle-value range can make black-versus-white identification uncertain, motivating comparison with the gray scale.
reference_purposes.Application: The scale is placed against the vehicle color until a step’s edge nearly disappears, then the corresponding identification color is selected.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Black is assigned through 40% gray and white above 40%; the red-logo alternative is confined to white vehicles.

ingredient.name: Vehicle paint-value comparator
ingredient.role: Resolve an uncertain foreground choice by comparing vehicle paint with a common gray scale.
ingredient.application: Place the scale against the vehicle color and find the step whose edge nearly disappears. Use black identification at 40% gray or lighter and white above 40%. A white vehicle may instead use a red logo with black text.
ingredient.scope: NASA-owned or leased vehicles under the 1976 manual’s section 7.1. The scale’s percentages express gray value, not a modern contrast ratio.
